teams.heading: Steve Borthwick faces scrutiny over progress two years into £264m investment
teams.body: Two years after the "historic" £264m Professional Game Partnership was signed to reshape the rugby landscape, Steve Borthwick’s side is yet to be described as world-leading. While the Premiership thrives commercially, the senior men's team remains under pressure with a World Cup only 12 months away. The deal allows Borthwick to award 25 enhanced contracts to assume more control over his players. However, analysis suggests the RFU prioritised collaboration over autonomy, leaving England's path to the top "answered in shades of grey."

teams.heading: Ireland women make six changes for Sunday fixture against Japan side
teams.body: Following last weekend’s narrow 40-36 loss to the USA, Ireland head coach Scott Bemand has shuffled his side for today's WXV Global Series encounter against Japan. teams.heading: Darcy Graham Ruled Out Of Scotland Autumn Tests With Bicep Rupture
teams.body: Scotland’s preparations for the autumn Tests have suffered a significant setback after Darcy Graham was ruled out for at least 12 weeks. The winger, who has scored 38 tries in 57 caps, sustained the injury during a friendly match for Edinburgh against Harlequins. Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt confirmed the diagnosis of a ruptured bicep, stating, “That’s not good news for us and not good news for him, especially with the autumn series coming up.”

teams.heading: Wales women seek back-to-back victories after dismantling South Africa side
teams.body: Following a clinical 50-19 victory over South Africa, the Wales women’s team returned to Cardiff Arms Park yesterday to face the USA. Head coach Sean Lynn targeted consecutive Test wins for the first time in his tenure, having reshuffled the backline to include Lleucu George at fly-half and the returning Carys Cox on the wing. Lynn noted that while losing Seren Lockwood to a head injury assessment was difficult, he remained excited to see the impact of his revamped half-back combination.

teams.heading: New Zealand women suffer last-gasp defeat against England at Twickenham
teams.body: The Black Ferns saw their unbeaten run ended in a 26-19 loss to England at the Allianz Stadium. Despite a resilient first-half performance that gave the visitors a 12-7 lead, New Zealand conceded a decisive interception try to Zoe Harrison in overtime. While Amy du Plessis, Ayesha Leti-I'iga and Mererangi Paul all crossed for the visitors, a second-half yellow card for Veisinia Mahutariki-Fakalelu hampered their momentum as the Red Roses secured the win.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus explains the specific role of his Springboks number eight
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has clarified his tactical approach to the back row, noting that the primary requirement for his number eight is the ability to scrummage in that position. With Marco van Staden starting at the back of the scrum against Australia, Erasmus emphasised that physical capability in the set-piece remains the defining factor for the role. “I know you guys probably get a bit frustrated with me, but you only scrum at number eight,” the head coach said.
